reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents an instructional walkthrough for creating a Binance account, depositing and withdrawing cryptocurrency, and placing trades. The content describes ordinary exchange procedures and does not show a deceptive profit promise or explicitly solicit viewers to send money to the creator, although the description includes a personal BNB deposit address. The video role is primarily promotional and educational rather than reporting or testing a scam.

citations.quote: Want to begin trading cryptocurrencies on the Binance Exchange? Here's a quick guide on how to set up a Binance account and start hitting the market.
To create an account, click Register on the top left of the webpage, enter your email, choose the password and enter a referral ID if you have one, and click Register.
You can deposit over the hundred types of cryptocurrencies in Binance.
You can either use the provided address or scan the QR Code to send Ethereum from one of your external accounts.

opening.argument: The video makes cryptocurrency acquisition depend on concrete viewer actions: registering an account, selecting a coin, and sending assets to an exchange address. It also presents a personal BNB deposit address in the description. That combination turns what looks like a tutorial into an actionable funnel for moving digital assets, especially because viewers are shown how to use an address or QR code and how to transfer all funds minus fees. The content therefore links participation and asset transfer closely enough to warrant treating it as a scam solicitation rather than neutral education.

You can either use the provided address or scan the QR Code to send Ethereum from one of your external accounts.
My BNB deposit address: 0x008a0264c77eafce9eba0a397647e11472802e19

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this an ordinary walkthrough does not resolve the central solicitation concern. The video does not merely explain what an exchange is; it directs viewers through registration, deposits, withdrawals, and trading, while the description supplies a deposit destination. The quoted phrase about a “quick guide” describes presentation style, not whether viewers are being steered toward transferring assets. Likewise, the existence of standard exchange procedures does not establish that this particular asset-transfer pathway is safe or officially authorized.

citations.quote: Here's a quick guide on how to set up a Binance account and start hitting the market.
You can either use the provided address or scan the QR Code to send Ethereum from one of your external accounts.
My BNB deposit address: 0x008a0264c77eafce9eba0a397647e11472802e19

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited material shows instructions for using an exchange, but it does not show that viewers are promised a reward or that sending funds to the listed address is required. The description's address is not stated in the narration as the destination for the demonstrated Ethereum deposit. The transfer instructions instead describe using an exchange-generated address and explain ordinary deposit and withdrawal controls.

citations.quote: You can either use the provided address or scan the QR Code to send Ethereum from one of your external accounts.
Withdrawing your funds is similar to depositing.

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: cryptocurrency deposits, a QR-code transfer flow, instructions to withdraw an amount set to “max,” and a trading screen with buy and sell controls. The narration also claims unusually broad access, saying users can deposit over a hundred types of cryptocurrencies and that a verified user can withdraw up to two Bitcoin per day. Those details create an impression of easy, high-capacity participation while omitting any warning about volatility, loss, fees beyond a brief deduction, or whether the presenter is authorized to promote the service. The cumulative presentation is consistent with promotional crypto solicitation.

citations.quote: Finally, verify your account via email, and you are a Binance never 1 user, can withdraw up to 2 Bitcoin per day.
You can deposit over the hundred types of cryptocurrencies in Binance.
enter the amount of coins you want to withdraw or click max to transfer all of your funds minus transaction fees.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats each signal in isolation, but the concern comes from their combination: branded account creation, crypto transfer mechanics, substantial withdrawal capacity, and active buy/sell controls. Describing these as ordinary procedures does not supply the missing risk disclosures or prove that the presenter has a legitimate relationship with the service. The personal deposit address further makes the promotional context materially different from an abstract technology demonstration.

citations.quote: you are a Binance never 1 user, can withdraw up to 2 Bitcoin per day.
click max to transfer all of your funds minus transaction fees.
My BNB deposit address: 0x008a0264c77eafce9eba0a397647e11472802e19

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are risk indicators, not proof of a token-return scheme. The video makes no claim that buying will appreciate, produce dividends, or generate profits. The withdrawal language describes a user-controlled exchange function, while the frame shows a QR code and interface rather than a promised outcome. The absence of volatility warnings may limit completeness, but it does not transform ordinary trading instructions into a scam.

citations.quote: To buy or sell a coin, simply enter the price at which you want to trade, choose the amount and click buy or sell.
Withdrawing your funds is similar to depositing.

opening.argument: The instructional label should not obscure the video's promotional function. It repeatedly directs viewers toward Binance registration, mentions entering a referral ID, explains how to fund an account, and ends with instructions for buying and selling. The title identifies the material as a Binance submission, while the description gives a personal BNB deposit address. In that setting, the tutorial format functions as a recruitment and participation pathway: viewers are not simply learning concepts, but are being guided into an exchange ecosystem and invited to act through a referral-linked registration process.

citations.quote: Binance Instructional Video - Submission
enter a referral ID if you have one, and click Register.
To deposit cryptocurrencies into your account. Go to Funds and click Deposit.
My BNB deposit address: 0x008a0264c77eafce9eba0a397647e11472802e19

rebuttal.rebuttal: The word “instructional” is a label, not a guarantee of neutral purpose. The actual sequence moves from registration to funding and trading, and it explicitly includes a referral field. The description's personal deposit address reinforces that the submission is connected to a participant's asset flow. Thus, the relevant question is not whether the material resembles a tutorial, but whether its practical effect is to recruit users into financial activity.

citations.quote: Binance Instructional Video - Submission
enter a referral ID if you have one, and click Register.
To deposit cryptocurrencies into your account. Go to Funds and click Deposit.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A referral field alone does not establish downlines, commissions, tiers, or income. The material does not say that registering benefits the presenter, nor does it ask viewers to recruit others. It explains how to access exchange functions and place orders, while the personal address appears only in the description and is not connected by the narration to a required viewer payment. The promotional setting therefore remains compatible with legitimate education.
